cards.text: Friend, John's Gospel opens like a song, and it starts before there was anything at all. "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God." And just so nobody misses it, John says it again: He was with God in the beginning.

cards.question: The Word was with God, and the Word was God. Through the Word, ___ things were made.

cards.text: ALL of it, baker, from every star in the sky down to every dust bunny in the back of my old junk drawer. And John says, "In Him was life, and that life was the light of men."
Then John says the Light shines in the darkness. Baker, I spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer. Me and darkness? First-name basis.

cards.question: John says the darkness has overcome the Light.

cards.text: Now a man shows up who was sent from God. His name was John, the one we know as John the Baptist (Matthew 3:1), and he came as a witness to testify about the Light.

cards.question: John the Baptist came to testify about the Light. Why?

answers.text: So everyone might believe through him
So people would come to follow him
So the temple leaders would listen

cards.question: John the Baptist was the Light himself.

cards.text: John the Baptist is like the sign out front of a bakery that says COOKIES. It points you right where to go, but friend, PLEASE don't try to eat the sign. The true Light, the one who gives light to everyone, was coming into the world.
He was in the world, and the world was made through Him.

cards.question: The world was made through the true Light, and now He's in it. What does the world do?

answers.text: It crowns Him as its king
It runs and hides from Him

cards.text: Picture a cookie looking up at the very stamper that made it and going, wait, have we MET? And it goes further: He came to His own, and His own did not receive Him.

cards.question: But to all who did receive the true Light and believed in His name, He gave the right to become ___ of God.
John says the children of God are born of blood or the will of man.

cards.text: They're born of God, friend. And now comes the line this whole song has been building to: "The Word became flesh and made His dwelling among us."

cards.question: John says, "We have seen His glory." Whose glory is it?

answers.text: The one and only Son from the Father
The great prophet sent from the Father
The mighty angel sent from the Father

cards.text: And He's full of grace and truth. Then John the Baptist cries out that the one who comes after him has surpassed him.

cards.question: John the Baptist says the one who comes after him has surpassed him because He was before him.

cards.text: And John says from His fullness we have all received grace upon grace. Picture an oven where one batch comes out and the next one is ALREADY right behind it. All day. Every day.

cards.question: The law was given through Moses, Israel's leader. Grace and truth came through ___.
John says no one has ever seen God. So who has made Him known?

cards.text: The Son, who is Himself God and is at the Father's side. That's how this song ends, friend: the Word who was with God in the beginning has made Him known.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 8 quotes "We have seen His glory.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The card says the Gospel is 'John's Gospel' and later cards say 'John says.' Who wrote this Gospel is a fact from outside the passage, since the text never names its writer, and the card gives no reference for it.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: 'And just so nobody misses it, John says it again' gives a reason for verse 2 that the text never states.

rule.text: Reasons: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: This story card is longer than 2 sentences: three sentences and a question fragment ('Then John says…', 'Baker, I spent YEARS…', 'Me and darkness?', 'First-name basis.').

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences and two beats: the sign joke about John 1:8 and the true Light coming into the world in John 1:9.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card cites John 1:8-9, but stop 2's range is John 1:9-18. Verse 8 belongs to stop 1, which already covered it in card 8.

rule.text: Each stop covers the next stretch of the passage, in order, and gives its verse range.

findings.problem: This story card is longer than 2 sentences: 'And John says…', 'Picture an oven…', 'All day.' and 'Every day.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Card 9 has John the Baptist crying out. Card 11 then begins 'And John says from His fullness we have all received grace upon grace,' and card 13 says 'John says no one has ever seen God.' A baker will likely hear verses 16 and 18 as John the Baptist's words, but the BSB closes his quote at the end of verse 15. The cards use 'John' for both the Gospel's narrator and John the Baptist.
findings.question: How should Papa Dorin refer to the narrator of John's Gospel so the baker can tell him apart from John the Baptist? For example, should he name the writer as John with a reference, say 'the writer,' or not name a speaker for narration at all?
